title: Chapter LX

teacherSummary.text: Elizabeth asks Darcy when he fell in love; he says he was in the middle before he knew he had begun. They discuss her impertinence. Darcy writes to Lady Catherine.

writingPrompts.label: Middle School
writingPrompts.text: In “Chapter LX,” how does Austen show reflections on love? Write a paragraph that states your claim, quotes two details from the chapter, and explains how each detail supports your idea. Use the characterization you noticed as one piece of evidence.

writingPrompts.label: High School / Common Core
writingPrompts.text: Analyze how Chapter LX develops the idea of reflections on love. Make a precise claim, support it with at least three pieces of textual evidence, and explain how the author's use of characterization and theme shapes that idea. Address one possible counterclaim.

writingPrompts.label: AP
writingPrompts.text: Write a literary argument in which you analyze how Jane Austen uses characterization in Chapter LX to complicate the reader's understanding of reflections on love. Develop a defensible thesis, select evidence purposefully, and explain how specific choices of diction and syntax create meaning.

writingPrompts.label: College Freshman
writingPrompts.text: Situate Chapter LX within its historical and literary context and argue how the chapter's treatment of reflections on love responds to that context. Engage with at least one secondary perspective (a critic, historian or the author's own statements), integrate quotations smoothly, and cite in MLA style.

writingPrompts.label: Graduate / PhD
writingPrompts.text: Develop an original argument that reads Chapter LX as a hinge in the novel's larger treatment of reflections on love. Position your reading within a named critical conversation (for example formalist, historicist, psychoanalytic, feminist or postcolonial approaches), account for the textual history where relevant, and articulate the stakes of your intervention for scholarship on Pride and Prejudice.

segments.activity: Quick-write and share on the opening question.
segments.script: Good morning, readers. Before we open the book, take three minutes and write your honest answer to this: What does Darcy's answer suggest about love? There is no wrong answer yet; we will test our ideas against the text today.

segments.activity: Model pronouncing, defining and using five key words in context.
segments.script: Today's words include evenness, overrated, parading, assiduously, obsequious. Watch how I figure out a word from its sentence before I check the dictionary. Here is the line: ““And if I had not a letter to write myself, I might sit by you, and admire the evenness of your writing, as another young lady once did.” My guess comes from the clues around it; the dictionary says: The state of being ven, level, or disturbed.

segments.activity: Present background, then the significance of the chapter.
segments.script: Let me give you some background that the first readers of Pride and Prejudice would have known. Courtship conversation allowed reflection on character. Now, why does this chapter matter? The answer emphasizes gradual, rational love over sudden passion. As you listen, jot one question you want answered.

segments.activity: Read the anchor passage aloud together; annotate for Characterization, Theme, Tone / mood.
segments.script: Let's read this passage together. I will read the first sentence; you track along. Every time you spot characterization, mark it. Turn to a partner: what does the author want us to notice here? I will collect three ideas on the board and we will choose the strongest one together, using the evidence.
